questions.stem: A tester notes angles 0°, 45°, 90°; which statement about transmission is correct?

questions.stem: Explain why frequency remains constant when light enters a new medium.

answer.exemplar: The wave's temporal oscillation is fixed by the source, and boundary conditions require the same frequency on both sides of the interface.

questions.explanation: The source sets the frequency; the medium changes wavelength and speed but not frequency.

questions.learningObjective: Explain why smaller grating spacing gives a larger first-order angle.
questions.stem: Explain why a grating with smaller spacing produces a larger first-order angle.

answer.exemplar: Bragg's law gives sinθ=λ/d, so reducing d increases the ratio and therefore the angle for fixed wavelength, provided the angle remains real.

questions.explanation: For fixed λ, smaller d raises λ/d, so θ=arcsin(λ/d) increases up to 90°.
questions.hint: Angle varies inversely with spacing.

questions.stem: A sprint review asks which statement about refractive index is correct; which is it?

options.text: Refractive index is the speed of light in the medium.

Refractive index is always less than one.
Refractive index is the ratio of vacuum speed to medium speed.

questions.explanation: n=c/v, so higher n means lower speed; n is dimensionless and at least one for ordinary media.
questions.hint: Index is vacuum speed divided by medium speed.
